name_en: Printing Woodblocks of the Tripiṭaka Koreana
hook: A library carved so carefully it became architecture.
summary_en: More than 80,000 Buddhist printing blocks, carved in Goryeo as a monumental act of preservation.
summary_ko: 고려가 새긴 8만여 장의 불교 경전 목판으로, 지식 보존의 거대한 시스템입니다.

images.credit: Wikimedia Commons CC0 image of Tripitaka Koreana at Haeinsa

sections.why_this_matters: For a code museum, the Tripiṭaka Koreana feels like an early data infrastructure: text, format, duplication, storage, and long-term preservation.
sections.what_you_are_looking_at: Each block carries carved characters in reverse for printing. The scale matters as much as the individual craft: tens of thousands of blocks had to remain consistent enough to transmit a complete canon.
sections.the_story: Carved during the Goryeo period, the woodblocks are kept at Haeinsa. They were made under conditions of crisis and devotion, turning religious text into a durable national archive.
